storyTagline: The Eagles go 17-0 again and edge the Chiefs 24-19 in Super Bowl CLIV for a fifth straight title, Ryland Maxwell runs the career rushing record out to 29,534 yards, and Dallas falls from streak breakers to 2-15.

stories.headline: Perfect Again: Eagles Go 17-0 and Hold Off the Chiefs 24-19 in Super Bowl CLIV
stories.dek: Philadelphia won all 20 of its games, had the league's best offense and its best defense, and needed every point of a 5-point Super Bowl margin for a fifth straight title.

stories.headline: Mad Max Puts the Career Rushing Record Out of Sight
stories.dek: Ryland Maxwell ran for 2,141 yards and 30 touchdowns, reached 29,534 career yards and passed Sherman Brandson at the top of the Career Legacy list.

stories.headline: The Doctor Wins a 5th MVP, and Akiem Brock Blocks His Way to a 7th Ring
stories.dek: Bones Crawford threw 52 touchdown passes in 18 games. Akiem Brock made 57 blocks, 19 more than any other lineman.

stories.headline: Wingo Takes Over in Philadelphia, and Viennes Finds New York Harder
stories.dek: Calvin Wingo II caught 114 passes for 2,267 yards and 25 touchdowns and was Offensive Player of the Year. Keenan Viennes, the winner a year ago, managed 726 yards for the 5-11-1 Jets.

stories.headline: From Streak Breakers to 2-15: Dallas Falls Apart
stories.dek: The Cowboys beat the champions twice in Y94. A year later they lost every home game and finished last in the power rankings.

stories.headline: The Chiefs Go 15-2 and Come Within 5 Points
stories.dek: Kansas City reached its first Super Bowl since Y79 behind Roc Dunkle's 40 touchdown passes and Maurice Vigil's league-leading 34 rushing scores.

stories.headline: Seventeen Meetings, Seventeen Losses: The Giants Still Cannot Beat Philadelphia
stories.dek: New York lost 32-31 and 24-15 to the Eagles in Y95. Since Y88 the series stands at 17-0, and Washington's losing run reached 8.

stories.headline: Travon Swaim, 34, Is Defensive Player of the Year at Last
stories.dek: The Lions' defensive back made 232 tackles in 20 games and helped a 9-8 club reach the conference final.

stories.headline: Rookies Who Did Not Wait: Herbig, Howell, Rosas and Jarrett
stories.dek: Bryant Herbig threw 30 touchdown passes for the 12-5 Commanders, Tee Rosas tied for the league lead in interceptions, and Payton Jarrett won a ring.

stories.headline: Two Interceptions From Hobbs: Brooker and Pettis Close In Together
stories.dek: Jamon Brooker and Lewis Pettis each have 41 career interceptions, 2 short of Damar Hobbs. Siran Spector moved to second on the rushing touchdown list.

takes.headline: Ryland Maxwell Has Passed Sherman Brandson. Stop Calling It a Debate.
takes.dek: Career Legacy 14,019 to 13,540, 12 rings to 10, and both career rushing records.

takes.headline: Keenan Viennes Was a Philadelphia Product, and the Jets Found Out the Hard Way
takes.dek: From 2,041 yards as Offensive Player of the Year to 726 in New York.

takes.headline: Calvin Wingo II Won Offensive Player of the Year With Ryland Maxwell's Touchdowns
takes.dek: Maxwell's touchdown catches fell from 53 to 7; Wingo's touchdowns rose from 7 to 25.

takes.headline: Bones Crawford Halved His Interceptions and Still Threw More Than Anyone. That Is Not an MVP Season.
takes.dek: 10 interceptions, 3 more than any other passer, and fewer yards than a 39-year-old Patriot.

takes.headline: We Said Dallas Had Philadelphia's Number. Dallas Went 2-15. The Rivalry Is Dead.
takes.dek: The worst record in the league, 0-8 at home, and two more losses to the Eagles.

takes.headline: The 14-3 Ravens Were the Luckiest Team in Football
takes.dek: A plus-54 point margin, 10-1 in one-score games and about 9.5 wins' worth of football.

takes.headline: Maurice Vigil Outscored Ryland Maxwell on the Ground, and Nobody Outside Kansas City Noticed
takes.dek: 34 rushing touchdowns to Maxwell's 30, the most in the league, at 34 years old.

takes.headline: Travon Swaim's Defensive Player of the Year Was a Lifetime Award, and He Earned It
takes.dek: 249 games for Detroit, a first trophy at 34, and a card that more than doubled.

takes.headline: The Buccaneers Were the Second-Best Team in the NFC, Whatever 10-7 Says
takes.dek: Plus-124 in points, 3-6 in one-score games, about 10.8 wins' worth of football.

takes.headline: Five Straight Titles, 17-0 and a 298-Point Margin: Philadelphia Has Broken the League
takes.dek: The best offense and the best defense in Y95, and only one Eagles game all year decided by a single point.

didYouKnow.text: Ryland Maxwell's Career Legacy of 14,019 is now the highest on file, ahead of Sherman Brandson's 13,540.
Ryland Maxwell has 12 rings and 6 Super Bowl MVPs, both the most on file. Dorren Skura coached him to every ring, with the Jets, the Falcons and the Eagles.
Bones Crawford threw the most interceptions in the league in Y94, 20, and again in Y95, 10. He was named MVP in Y95 anyway.
The Cowboys lost all 8 of their home games in Y95, a year after ending the Eagles' 49-game winning streak.
The 15-2 Chiefs lost only to the 8-9 Cardinals and the 6-11 Raiders, two clubs with losing records.
The Giants have met Dorren Skura's Eagles 17 times since Y88 and lost all 17.
Rookie tight end Ulysees Howell caught 107 passes for the Commanders and averaged 5.1 yards a catch.
Landon Irwin of the Lions led the league with 5 sacks in Y95. No other player had more than 3.
Payton Jarrett's 1,450 receiving yards as a rookie were the second most in the league, behind only his teammate Calvin Wingo II.
Y95 was the 13th unbeaten season of Dorren Skura's career. His Eagles had also gone 17-0 two seasons earlier, in Y93.
Jamon Brooker is 2 interceptions behind Damar Hobbs's league record for career interceptions (43): 95% of the way there.
Siran Spector is 33 rushing TDs behind Lane McCoy's league record for career rushing TDs (458): 93% of the way there.

All 23 Defensive Player of the Year awards on league cards belong to defensive backs. The game credits a corner or safety's stop on a pass play as an interception, and the award rating counts each interception as much as 6 tackles. Jayon Queen leads with 2 awards.

Defensive linemen have 96 career interceptions in 8,718 games, one every 91 games; defensive backs pick one off every 9.5 games. The game scores a lineman's stop on a pass play as a sack: linemen have 399 sacks, defensive backs 1.
Retro Bowl caps each draft class by the coach's last record. After Skura's Eagles went 17-0 in Y95 (100%), prospects 5 to 50 of the Y96 class could rate at most 3 stars; a .500 season allows 3.5.
Winning shrinks the draft: in 72 of Skura's 77 seasons that fed a draft at the same club, his record capped the next class at 3 stars or less.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Sherman Brandson
vault.text: The General never flinched. Career Legacy 13,540, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Rondale Ikarras
vault.text: Flashy, loud, unstoppable, and he knew it. He was that guy. Career Legacy 11,329, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · God Johnson
vault.text: He changed his name to God. Then he earned it. Career Legacy 12,708, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jayon Queen
vault.text: Two Defensive Player of the Year awards. Only one other player in this league has ever matched that. Career Legacy 8,732, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Tyrone Baugh
vault.text: Seven seasons, seven championships, and Tyrone Baugh has a ring for every one of them. Career Legacy 8,436, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Levante Hopkins
vault.text: The quiet one who did the dirty work. Career Legacy 11,408, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Mose Junior
vault.text: Some players chase rings. Mose Junior chased ball carriers. Career Legacy 7,737, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Dennis Baylon
vault.text: Seven trips to the Super Bowl. Seven rings. Not one loss. Career Legacy 10,385, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Charlie John
vault.text: Seven straight Super Bowls. Charlie John was there for every one of them. Career Legacy 10,071, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Ian Finney
vault.text: The first superstar. The Infinity Man. Career Legacy 11,363, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Bilal Tolbert
vault.text: No individual trophies. Four rings. And a sack record nobody has caught. Career Legacy 8,458, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Wayne Wilson
vault.text: Four hundred thirty-one games. Nobody in this league has played longer. Career Legacy 9,490, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Cairo Asanjh
vault.text: Some players chase records. Cairo Asanjh chased Ian Finney. Career Legacy 10,320, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jahmyr Gibbs
vault.text: Mr. Incredible was here at the start, and he set the bar high. Career Legacy 7,655, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Zander Kolar
vault.text: Some defensive linemen are measured in sacks. Zander Kolar was measured in tackles. Career Legacy 8,665, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Ray Waller
vault.text: Never count out a man whose nickname is a promise. Career Legacy 8,900, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Tyler Pacheco
vault.text: Tyler Pacheco never needed the big play. He needed the ball, and he got it. Career Legacy 7,837, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Lukas Russell
vault.text: The Running Man started fast and never slowed down. Career Legacy 9,312, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Taron Hayes
vault.text: Eleven tackles a game, for 213 games, and two Defensive Player of the Year awards. Career Legacy 7,142, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Nick Bolton
vault.text: One of the originals, and he never stopped tackling. Career Legacy 8,731, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Michael Wilson
vault.text: Wayne's brother, and nobody's afterthought. Career Legacy 8,760, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jackson Wardell Kline
vault.text: Tyrion Kline's son did not live in anyone's shadow. He built his own. Career Legacy 10,090, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Malakai Sawyer
vault.text: Some backs have a great season. Malakai Sawyer keeps having them. Career Legacy 7,540, Y88 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · K'Lavon Settle
vault.text: Fifteen seasons in San Francisco, and nobody on a card has made more tackles. Career Legacy 7,748, Y88 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Daren Teamer
vault.text: Eleven tackles a game is a Hall of Fame habit, and Daren Teamer has never broken it. Career Legacy 8,273, Y89 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Kalif Suh
vault.text: A Jets linebacker since Y76, and the middle of that defense has rarely moved without him. Career Legacy 9,252, Y92 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jakeem Friend
vault.text: Linemen do not win trophies. Jakeem Friend won seven rings instead. Career Legacy 9,462, Y93 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Lane McCoy
vault.text: Every time Denver got close to the goal line, the whole league knew who was getting the ball. Career Legacy 6,516, Y93 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Damar Hobbs
vault.text: No defender in league history has taken the ball away through the air more often than Damar Hobbs. Career Legacy 8,410, Y93 class.
